title: Extract first and last items
prompt:
You have a list of items. Return an object with `first` and `last` fields containing the first and last items from the list.

For the sample, `["apple", "banana", "cherry"]` should produce `{"first": "apple", "last": "cherry"}`.
hints: Two fields: `first` is payload[0], and `last` is... the last item. In DataWeave, negative indices count from the end.
The last item is at index -1. You do not need to calculate the size; just use the negative index directly.
Think about what happens if the array is empty: payload[0] would be null, and payload[-1] would also be null. That is actually correct behavior for this task.

mustFail.why: uses both array index and slice, returning arrays instead of scalars
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{first: payload[0 to 0], last: payload[-1 to -1]}

explanation.approach: Index the first element with [0] and the last with [-1]. Negative indices count backward from the end, so -1 is always the last item. You do not need to know the array length.

snippets.label: The answer
snippets.note: Index [0] is the first item, [-1] is the last. No size calculation needed.

snippets.label: Negative indexing: -1 is the last
snippets.note: Negative indices count from the end. -1 is the last, -2 is second-to-last, etc.

snippets.label: An index past the end is null
snippets.note: Out-of-bounds access does not throw an error; it just returns null. This is useful for defensive coding.

snippets.label: A range is different from an index
snippets.note: [0] returns the item itself, [0 to 0] returns an array with one item. For this task, you want [0] and [-1], not ranges.

snippets.label: sizeOf tells you the length
snippets.note: sizeOf returns the count. But for the last item, negative indexing is simpler than calculating sizeOf(payload) - 1.

snippets.label: Why the tempting alternative is wrong
snippets.note: Both return the same value, but negative indexing is clearer — it says 'get the last' without asking you to do arithmetic.

snippets.label: There is no negative zero
snippets.note: Counting back from the end starts at -1, not -0, because -0 and 0 are the same number. So `[-0]` quietly gives you the FIRST element — the one place where reaching for the end lands you at the start.
